text:
jordan: Quick sweep — attaching the latest console chart screenshot. I want a short list of what to change before we ship: legend placement, axis units, smoothing copy, and how we flag outliers for screen readers. Screenshot: https://files.redwood.ai/ux/chart-annot-v3.png

anita: On copy — can we avoid jargon. Instead of "Smoothed"/"Raw" maybe "7-sample smoothing" and "No smoothing". Users misinterpret "raw" as broken. Also: the smoothing toggle should show sample size on hover.

sam: Implementation note — legend currently uses a flex wrap that collapses on narrow widths, causing height jumps. We can do a single-line truncate -> popover for overflow. Example CSS: ```
.legend { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
.legend-popover { max-width: 280px; }
```
But this won't help keyboard access unless we add a visible focus target.

lee: Design idea — move the legend into a collapsible rail on mobile so it doesn't overlap annotations. For axis units, prefer explicit SI suffixes (e.g., "k", "M") and show exact value on hover tooltip. For accessibility, show unit in the aria-label for the axis: "Requests per second (rps)" is clearer than just "rps".

chris: Metrics concern — support tickets show users confusing percentages and absolute counts. Can we add a small unit toggle in the top-right (%, count)? That should cut the confusion. Also +1 for showing the smoothing parameter in the control itself, not buried in a tooltip.

wanda: A11y nits: color contrast for the outlier marker is 2.9:1 vs background — fail. Use >=4.5:1 for small markers or add a thicker stroke. Focus order: legend popover is not reachable by keyboard right now. For screen readers, call out outliers as: "Outlier at 12:04 — 13,400 requests (2.1% above baseline)". Add role="list" -> role="listitem" for legend entries so NVDA reads them as a group.

anita: Small microcopy tweak — instead of "Show smoothing" label, try "Smoothing: 7-sample" with a caret to open options. Less modal, more descriptive at a glance.

sam: Technical tradeoff: default smoothing off is cheaper (less background compute for previews). If product wants smoothing on by default we need to budget for caching. Also outlier detection currently uses z-score with threshold 3; we could expose a "sensitivity" slider but that risks clutter.

lee: UX compromise — keep smoothing default off, but persist the last user choice per-org. For outliers, show faint ghost markers for points filtered by smoothing so users see where the algorithm changed the curve. 

chris: Agree on persist-by-org. Also add a short tooltip copy for the sensitivity control: "Higher sensitivity highlights more deviations; lower sensitivity ignores small blips."

wanda: Example aria snippet for an outlier button: ```html
<button aria-label="Outliers: 3 flagged. Press to open outlier details" aria-expanded="false">Outliers</button>
```
Make sure the details list has aria-describedby linking to the chart summary.

jordan: Great recs — summary for engineering/design: 1) Legend: single-line truncate + popover + keyboard focus; mobile collapsible rail. 2) Copy: "Smoothing: 7-sample / No smoothing" visible; persist choice. 3) Units: SI suffix + explicit unit in aria. 4) Outliers: higher contrast marker, aria phrasing like wanda suggested, and optional sensitivity in advanced settings. 5) Avoid default smoothing on to save compute.

deploy-bot: Created ticket https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4122 to track the changes (assignee: sam).
